from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Setting", [
            "Imagine points scattered across a plane.", 
            "A line pivots around one point.", 
            "It sweeps until it hits another.", 
            "This process repeats indefinitely.", 
            "This creates the windmill motion."
        ])
        
        # Points
        points_data = [
            'B2', 'B5', 'C4', 'D2', 'E4'
        ]
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid[pos], color=WHITE) for pos in points_data])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.play(FadeIn(points))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        pivot = points[0]
        line = Line(start=pivot.get_center() + LEFT*2, end=pivot.get_center() + RIGHT*2, color=BLUE)
        line.rotate(about_point=pivot.get_center(), angle=0.5)
        self.play(Create(line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF6347")
        # Rotating until it hits points[1]
        target_angle = angle_between_vectors(line.get_vector(), points[1].get_center() - pivot.get_center())
        self.play(Rotate(line, angle=target_angle, about_point=pivot.get_center()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#7FFF00")
        # Highlight points
        self.play(Indicate(points[0]), Indicate(points[1]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Shift pivot to point[1]
        new_pivot = points[1]
        new_line = Line(start=new_pivot.get_center() + DOWN, end=new_pivot.get_center() + UP, color=BLUE)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(line, new_line))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Core Insight: Periodicity and Convex Hull", [
            "The line visits every point pair.",
            "Rotation is periodic and cyclic.",
            "It reveals the convex hull.",
            "Matches the rotating calipers algorithm.",
            "An elegant geometric structure emerges."
        ])

        points = [
            np.array([0, 1, 0]), np.array([1, 1.5, 0]), np.array([2, 0.5, 0]),
            np.array([1.5, -1, 0]), np.array([0.5, -0.5, 0]), np.array([-0.5, 0, 0])

        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(p, color=BLUE) for p in points])
        self.place_in_area(dots, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        hull = Polygon(dots[0].get_center(), dots[1].get_center(), dots[2].get_center(), 
                       dots[3].get_center(), dots[4].get_center(), dots[5].get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        
        line = Line(start=np.array([-3, 0, 0]), end=np.array([3, 0, 0]), color=WHITE)
        line.rotate(PI/4, about_point=np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Create(dots))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Create(hull))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Create(line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), line.animate.rotate(PI/2, about_point=np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0])))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF4500"), line.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion & Application", ["Windmill motion shows geometric stability.", "Useful for robot path planning.", "Efficient collision detection logic."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Windmill motion shows geometric stability.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        windmill_center = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        arm = Line(ORIGIN, UP*1.5, color=WHITE)
        windmill = VGroup(windmill_center, arm)
        self.place_at_grid(windmill, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(windmill))
        self.play(Rotate(arm, angle=PI/2, about_point=windmill_center.get_center()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Useful for robot path planning.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        robot_path = VMobject(color=RED)
        robot_path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid['C2'], self.grid['C5'], self.grid['E5'], self.grid['E2']])
        self.play(Create(robot_path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Efficient collision detection logic.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        obs1 = Square(side_length=0.5, color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(self.grid['D3'])

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Windmill Problem (Computational Geometry & Convex Hulls)

sections.title: Introduction: The Setting
sections.content: Define the windmill problem: n points in a plane, with a line passing through one point acting as a pivot. The line rotates until it hits another point, then pivots around that new point, continuing indefinitely.
sections.example: Visualize a group of n fireflies (points) in a dark forest. A laser beam (the line) pivots around one firefly until it illuminates another, creating a rhythmic, rotating motion.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Angular Sweeping
sections.content: Explain the concept of angular velocity and the 'sweep' operation. Introduce how we sort points by their polar angle relative to the pivot point to determine the next collision point.
sections.example: Imagine a radar screen scanning clockwise; the moment the radar beam touches a firefly, that becomes the new center of rotation.

sections.title: The Mechanical Logic: State Transitions
sections.content: Explain the step-by-step logic: (1) Identify current pivot P1 and point P2. (2) Calculate angles of all other points relative to P1. (3) Choose the point that requires the smallest clockwise rotation. (4) Update P1 to this new point.
sections.example: A mechanical windmill where the blade is a rigid rod. As it hits a pin (point), the rod's rotation center shifts to that pin, mimicking a 'bouncing' or 'revolving' motion.

sections.title: Core Insight: Periodicity and Convex Hull
sections.content: Discuss the 'Invariance' principle: The line covers every possible pair of points. Prove that the rotation is cyclic and the set of edges visited relates to the rotating calipers algorithm used in convex hulls.
sections.example: An animation showing the laser beam tracing all possible diagonals of the set of points, effectively 'knitting' the entire convex structure of the shape.

sections.title: Conclusion & Application
sections.content: Summarize how this illustrates geometric stability and algorithmic complexity. Connect it to real-world applications like path planning and collision detection.
sections.example: Using the windmill logic to design a robot arm that moves between targets in a crowded room without crossing pre-set boundaries.
